topic: Structure and Functions of NITI Aayog
description: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is the premier policy think tank of the Government of India. It replaced the erstwhile Planning Commission in 2015 and operates primarily on the principle of cooperative federalism.

sections.title: Establishment and Background
sections.description: The history of NITI Aayog's formation and its foundational framework.

key_concepts.explanation: An intellectual platform or institute that provides directional, strategic, and technical advice to the government on various policy matters.
Unlike the Planning Commission's 'top-down' model, NITI Aayog ensures the active participation of all states and local bodies in policy formulation, starting from the village level to the center.

historical_events.significance: Established to formulate and implement Five-Year Plans for India's economic development; it was later replaced by NITI Aayog.
Formed via a Union Cabinet resolution as a non-constitutional and non-statutory body to serve as the government's premier think tank.

sections.title: Administrative Structure
sections.description: The key office bearers and the composition of various councils under NITI Aayog.

key_associations.extra_info: The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
Enjoys the rank and status of a Cabinet Minister.
Appointed for a fixed tenure and enjoys the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

key_associations.associated_with: All Chief Ministers and Lt. Governors
key_associations.extra_info: Provides a platform to discuss and finalize the national development agenda with the active involvement of states.
Formed on a need basis to address specific contingencies or issues impacting more than one state or a particular region.

important_facts.fact: The first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog was Arvind Panagariya, and the first CEO was Sindhushree Khullar.

sections.title: Core Principles
sections.description: The guiding philosophies that direct the functioning and policymaking of NITI Aayog.

key_concepts.explanation: The recognition that strong states make a strong nation. It promotes continuous cooperation and partnership between the central and state governments.
Encouraging healthy competition among states through various indices and rankings to improve their socio-economic and governance performance.

sections.title: Key Hubs and Functions
sections.description: The main ideational and executive pillars through which NITI Aayog operates.

key_concepts.explanation: Acts as the primary interface between the states and the central government, ensuring that states have a say in national policymaking.
Builds the think tank capabilities of NITI Aayog by promoting research, maintaining a state-of-the-art resource center, and sharing best practices.

important_facts.fact: Unlike the erstwhile Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not possess the power to allocate funds to ministries or state governments; this power strictly resides with the Ministry of Finance.

sections.title: Major Initiatives and Indices
sections.description: Key programs and indices launched by NITI Aayog to measure development and foster innovation.

key_associations.extra_info: Promotes scientific temper and innovation among students through Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) in schools across India.
Aims to rapidly transform 112 of India's least developed districts by improving key socio-economic indicators.
Evaluates and ranks the progress of States and Union Territories on the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals.
Ranks states based on their incremental improvements and overall performance in health outcomes.
